RIPPED MOUNTAIN DEBRIS PACK

Five transparent PNG overlays in the matching terracotta Indian folk-mural style.

01-wide-torn-earth-hanging-roots.png
Attach directly under the lifted mountain. Let the rocky top edge overlap the existing underside by 10 to 25 pixels so the join disappears.

02-uprooted-falling-tree.png
Large tree for the left or right side. Keep it behind Ravan and scale to about 18 to 28 percent of the viewport width.

03-falling-broken-tree.png
Second tree facing the opposite direction. Place at another depth and slightly reduce saturation or opacity.

04-soil-rock-root-cascade.png
Place directly beneath the center of the floating mountain. It already includes soil, roots, boulders and pebbles.

05-falling-branches-leaves.png
Use as the nearest atmospheric overlay. It may sit partly in front of the central art, but keep important faces clear.

SUGGESTED SCROLL ANIMATION
- Hanging roots: fixed to the lifted mountain; move together with it.
- Large tree: downward 30 to 60 px with 3 to 5 degrees of rotation.
- Broken tree: downward 45 to 80 px with opposite 3 to 6 degree rotation.
- Soil and rocks: downward 80 to 140 px at a slightly faster rate.
- Branches and leaves: downward 120 to 180 px with very gentle sideways drift.

Keep movement slow and scroll-controlled. Do not loop the debris continuously; it should feel like one suspended epic moment.
